The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the Titanic.

To understand blockchain technology, imagine a massive, shared notebook that is kept by thousands of people all over the world instead of just one person or one bank. In a traditional system, like a bank ledger, only the bank has the official record of your transactions, and they can change it if they want to. In a blockchain, however, everyone has a copy of this notebook.

If someone tries to write a new entry or change an old one, they can't just do it on their own copy. They have to shout out the change to everyone else. The other people check their own notebooks to see if the new entry makes sense and follows the rules. If the majority agrees that the change is valid, then everyone updates their own copy at the same time. Because there are so many copies and everyone has to agree, it is nearly impossible for a hacker to sneak in and change the records without being noticed. This makes the system extremely secure and trustworthy, as no single person or group controls the data.
